'''Peter Landrock''' (born August 20, 1948 in [[Horsens]]) is a Danish [[cryptographer]] and mathematician. He is known for his contributions to data [[encryption]] methods and codes.<ref name="EPO about Peter Landrock" /> Landrock has been active since the 1970s as research scientist and faculty member for [[Cambridge University]] and the [[University of Aarhus]] and others, and was active for [[Microsoft]] and [[Cryptomathic]].<ref name="Niels Bohr Inst Peter landrock">{{cite web|title=NBIA Colloquium by Peter Landrock "Cryptographic Techniques in Electronic Communication Today and Tomorrow "|url=http://www.nbi.ku.dk/english/Calendar/activities_15/nbiacolloquium20_03_2015landrock/|publisher=Niels Bohr Institute|access-date=2015-05-15|archive-date=2015-06-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150611194945/http://www.nbi.ku.dk/english/Calendar/activities_15/nbiacolloquium20_03_2015landrock/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="Isaac Newton Institute Peter landrock">{{cite web|title=A Personal Perspective|url=http://www.newton.ac.uk/files/reports/casestudies/landrock.pdf|publisher=The Isaac Newton Institute|accessdate=15 May 2015}}</ref> He has been visiting professor at [[Oxford University]], [[Katholieke Universiteit Leuven|Leuven University]]<ref name="CFIR on Landrock">{{cite web|title=Munich and Denmark: Finance and IT Across Borders – Keynotes|url=http://www.cfir.dk/en-GB/munich/munich/Pages/Keynotes.aspx|website=CFIR|publisher=Copenhagen Fintech Innovation and Research|accessdate=15 May 2015}}</ref> and [[Princeton University]].<ref name="Princeton Peter Landrock">{{cite web|title=Institute for Advanced Study|url=https://www.ias.edu/people/cos/users/5017|website=www.ias.edu|accessdate=3 June 2015}}</ref>

==Background and career==
Landrock obtained a diploma in mathematics and physics in 1972 from the [[University of Aarhus]]. He received his Ph.D. in mathematics from the [[University of Chicago]] in 1974<ref name="Bloomberg on Peter Landrock">{{cite web|title=Executive Profile – Peter Landrock|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/person.asp?personId=53336464&privcapId=28494880|website=Bloomberg Business|publisher=Bloomberg L.P.|accessdate=15 May 2015}}</ref> for his research on elementary [[abelian group|abelian]] and [[dihedral group|dihedral]] defect groups, under [[George Glauberman|George Isaac Glauberman]] and [[Richard Dagobert Brauer]].<ref name="Mathematics Genealogy on Peter Landrock">{{cite web|title=Peter Landrock|url=http://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=6692|website=Mathematics Genealogy Project|publisher=Department of Mathematics North Dakota State University|accessdate=15 May 2015}}</ref> In 1975, Landrock became associate Professor in the Department of Mathematics at [[Aarhus University]], then full Professor. From 1982 until 1983, Landrock was visiting professor at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] in Princeton, New Jersey.<ref name="Princeton Peter Landrock" />

In 1986 he founded the company [[Cryptomathic]] together with [[Ivan Damgård]].  It was his research work on [[cryptography]] and [[coding theory]] at the [[Isaac Newton Institute]], which inspired him to shift the focus of his work to corporate research at Cryptomathic,<ref name="Isaac Newton Institute Peter landrock" /><ref name="Bloomberg on Peter Landrock" /> where he joined forces with researchers such as [[Vincent Rijmen]] and [[Whitfield Diffie]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cryptomathic.com/company/management-team |title=Cryptomathic Management Team |accessdate=2013-04-05 |archive-date=2013-03-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130308165733/http://www.cryptomathic.com/company/management-team |url-status=dead }}</ref>

By 1996 he had joined the Isaac Newton Institute, Cambridge University as Research Program Organizer, and since 1997, Landrock has been senior member of the [[Wolfson College, Cambridge]] University.<ref name="Niels Bohr Inst Peter landrock" /><ref name="Isaac Newton Institute Peter landrock" /> Landrock has been member of the Danish IT Security Council as adviser to the Danish Government<ref name="Bloomberg on Peter Landrock" /> from 1999 to 2007.
From 1997 until 2010, Landrock was as a Member of Microsoft's Technical Advisory Board in Cambridge and has also served as a member of the board of the [[Villum Foundation]] in Copenhagen since 2008. In 2014 Landrock became Member of the Technical Advisory Board of the Turing Gateway of Mathematics at Cambridge University.<ref name="Niels Bohr Inst Peter landrock" /> In 2021, he was elected a By-Fellow of [[Churchill College, Cambridge]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Professor Peter Landrock|url=https://www.chu.cam.ac.uk/fellows/peter-landrock-2/|website=Churchill College|accessdate=18 July 2022}}</ref>

==Cryptography==
Landrock was President of the [[International Association for Cryptologic Research]] from 1992 to 1995<ref name="Niels Bohr Inst Peter landrock" /> and General Chair at the [[Eurocrypt]] conference for cryptography research in 1990.<ref name="Eurocrypt Peter Landrock">{{cite web|title=History of IACR Conferences and Workshops|url=https://www.iacr.org/conferences/history.html|publisher=International Association for Cryptologic Research}}</ref> In 1996 he was one of the organizers of a research programme in Cryptography at the Newton Institute at University of Cambridge.<ref name="Niels Bohr Inst Peter landrock" /> The term "What You See Is What You Sign" ([[WYSIWYS]]) was coined in 1998 by Landrock and Torben P. Pedersen of Cryptomathic during their work on delivering secure and legally binding digital signatures for Pan-European projects.<ref>P. Landrock, T. Pedersen, "WYSIWYS? – What you see is what you sign?". Information Security Technical Report, Volume 3, Number 2, 1998, pp. 55–61</ref>

Landrock contributed to more than twenty entries to the ''[[Encyclopedia of Cryptography and Security]]'' including articles on [[PKCS]], [[Secure Shell|SSH]], [[public key infrastructure]] and [[certificate authority|certificate authorities]].<ref name="dblp – Peter Landrock">{{cite web|title=Peter Landrock|url=http://dblp.uni-trier.de/pers/hd/l/Landrock:Peter|website=dblp|publisher=dblp – Computer Science Bibliography|accessdate=15 May 2015}}</ref> His research focus since the late 1980s included subject areas as [[Key management]] systems,<ref name="IEEE Key Mgt Landrock">{{cite journal|last1=Fumy|first1=W.|last2=Landrock|first2=P.|title=Principles of key management|journal=IEEE Journal on Selected Areas in Communications|date=1993|volume=11 |issue=5 |pages=785–793|doi=10.1109/49.223881}}</ref> [[EMV]] and Card Payment Solutions<ref name="Encyclopedia payment card- Landrock">{{cite book|last1=Landrock|first1=P.|last2=van Tilborg (Ed.)|first2=H.C.A.|title=Payment Card, in: Encyclopedia of Cryptography and Security|date=2005|publisher=Springer|isbn=978-0-387-23473-1}}</ref> and [[Authentication]].<ref name="LectureNotes Authent Landrock">{{cite journal|last1=Brant|first1=J.|last2=Damgård|first2=I.|last3=Landrock|first3=P.|last4=Pedersen|first4=T.|title=Zero-Knowledge Authentication Scheme with Secret Key Exchange in: Advances in Cryptology – CRYPTO' 88|journal=IEEE Lecture Notes in Computer Science|date=1990|volume=403|pages=583–588|doi=10.1007/0-387-34799-2_43 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

He has lectured on cryptography at more than 150 Universities. The [[European Patent Office]] recognized that Landrock's “inventions have helped secure electronic voting systems and electronic passport solutions”.<ref name="EPO about Peter Landrock">{{cite web|title=Master of the Puzzles|url=http://www.epo.org/news-issues/european-inventor/finalists/2010/landrock.html|website=www.EPO.org|publisher=European Patent Office|accessdate=15 May 2015|archive-date=17 October 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121017144750/http://www.epo.org/news-issues/european-inventor/finalists/2010/landrock.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Awards and recognition==
In 1991 Landrock was awarded the Danish Data Security Prize, and in 2004, Landrock received the BIT Price for engineering entrepreneurship from the Danish Engineers.<ref name="DKCERT PRICE LANDROCK">{{cite web|title=INGENIØRPRIS TIL KRYPTERINGSEKSPERT|url=https://www.cert.dk/nyheder/nyheder.shtml?04-03-17-17-09-44|website=DKCERT Danish Computer Security Incident Response Team|publisher=DKCERT, DeIC|accessdate=22 May 2015}}</ref>

His achievements with Cryptomathic were recognised by the [[World Economic Forum]] in 2003 and he received the [[Visa Inc.|VISA]] Smart Start Award for the work on Chip and Pin.<ref name="Isaac Newton Institute Peter landrock" /> In 2010, Landrock was named a finalist for European Inventor 2010 in the "Lifetime Achievement" category by the [[European Patent Office]] stating that many of today’s established data encryption methods and codes “bear the mark of ... Peter Landrock”<ref name="EPO about Peter Landrock"/>

In July 2019, Landrock was awarded the degree of Doctor of Science honoris causa for his lifetime achievement in cryptographic technology.<ref name="DrHC-Bristol">{{cite web |last1=Crane |first1=Edward |title=Peter Landrock - Graduation |url=http://www.bristol.ac.uk/graduation/honorary-degrees/honorary-graduates-2019/peter-landrock/ |publisher=University of Bristol |accessdate=16 October 2019}}</ref>
